description: ETag-versioned cache for the WorkflowRun status read path: skip the full State deserialize when State has not changed since the last read, while keeping definition and artifact resolution live-fresh and the cache bounded.

tasks.title: ETag-versioned WorkflowRun aggregate cache for status reads
tasks.description: Add a bounded singleton WorkflowRunStatusCache (ISingletonService) keyed by workflowRunId holding (ETag, deserialized WorkflowRun) with a FIFO entry cap. Rework WorkflowQuerier.GetStatusAsync to first read the row ETag as a scalar projection (EF.Property<long>(e, "ETag"), no State materialization), serve the cached aggregate on an ETag match without executing the full typed deserialization of State (JSON.Deserialize<WorkflowRun>), and on a miss load the full row, Hydrate (including RestoreStoredEpicNumber), and store the entry under the new ETag. Definition resolution (WorkflowDefinitionResolver.LoadTemplateAsync), WorkflowStatusMapper.BuildStatusView, and artifact attachment remain per call so live profile edits and new artifacts stay fresh; definition resolution's lightweight State reads (profile-id extraction) are accepted residual scope (see design D1 scope note). Introduce a deserialization seam (e.g. an injectable/countable WorkflowRun deserializer, or make the deserialize path observable) so cost tests can assert full-typed-deserialize counts without wall-clock. Treat the cached WorkflowRun as a read-only shared snapshot (no caller mutates it).
acceptanceCriteria: Two successive GetStatusAsync calls with no WorkflowRunStore write between them return equivalent views, and the second call executes the full typed deserialization of State (JSON.Deserialize<WorkflowRun>) zero times (asserted via a deserialization counter/probe, not timing).

After a WorkflowRunStore save increments ETag, the next GetStatusAsync executes the full typed deserialization of State exactly once, returns a view reflecting the written State, and stores it under the new ETag; subsequent reads at the same ETag execute that deserialization zero times.

A view served from a cache hit for ETag N is field-by-field equal (Status, CurrentStage, stages, tasks, checks, approval, failure, pending work, artifact summaries) to a view produced by forcing a full rebuild at the same ETag N.
GetStatusAsync for an unknown workflowRunId returns null and creates no cache entry.

An artifact recorded for a task run after the most recent State write (ETag unchanged) appears in the returned view's artifact summaries, and is present on two successive reads; the full typed deserialization of State does not execute solely because artifacts changed.
The cache enforces a bounded entry count with eviction; after evicting an entry, a later read for that run returns an equivalent rebuilt view (correctness holds on eviction).

A test asserts the cached WorkflowRun aggregate is not mutated by BuildStatusView, AttachArtifactSummariesAsync, or any per-call read path — the shared singleton snapshot stays read-only across request scopes (the design's shared-mutable-aggregate risk mitigation).

Existing StatusSpecs and WorkflowStructureSpecs pass unchanged, proving the WorkflowStatusView? contract shape and null semantics are preserved and no caller (WorkflowRoutes*, IssueGrain, WorkflowActivityQuerier, AgentActivityFeedAssembler) required changes.
New specs are placed with the existing querier status tests; the deserialization-cost assertions follow design/testing.md §5 (count operations, never wall-clock; unit < 50ms, spec < 500ms).
`npm run build` (dotnet build Mohist.sln) succeeds with no warnings (TreatWarningsAsErrors acts as lint), and `npm test` (server) passes.
tasks.output: Singleton WorkflowRunStatusCache + reworked WorkflowQuerier.GetStatusAsync (read-ETag-then-hit/miss) + deserialization-counting seam + spec tests covering hit/miss/equivalence/contract-null/artifact-freshness/boundedness, all green.
tasks.notes: Design: openspec/changes/issue-539/design.md (D1 cache the aggregate only, not the assembled view; D2 singleton injected into scoped querier; D3 ETag-equality validation, no TTL/wall-clock; D4 bounded FIFO; D5 accept rare concurrent first-miss redundant deserialize). No schema/EF migration and no change to WorkflowRunStore's ETag increment rule. Shadow-property projection via EF.Property<long>(e, "ETag") is the standard EF Core form; if the SQLite provider blocks it in a Select, fall back to FindAsync + Entry(...).Property<long>("ETag") on the miss path only. An optional config kill switch that bypasses the cache (falls back to today's unconditional deserialize) is cheap to add but not required for correctness; include only if it adds no extra surface.
